rulings_this_validation_makes.useful: every template carries the citation, the printed location and value it rests on, what the arithmetic returns, why the confidence class is limited, the unresolved qualifications, and the distinction between the report's assertion and verified truth

templates.template_when_it_applies: both facts are PRESENT and the elapsed days exceed the derived six-year span
templates.the_fixture_is: a record whose arithmetic exceeds the six-year span
templates.rendered_explanation: Consumer Reporting Act (Nova Scotia), R.S.N.S. 1989, c. 93, s. 10(3)(c). the printed label, its pages and its value, quoted from the presentation as the fact model records them: the field the register records as "Last Payment Date of the debt record" printed at row label "Last Payment Date" inside a collection record, PDF page 16 (and the continued record on PDF page 17), and the field recorded as "Report reference date" printed at label "Request Date" in the page header, with the same value on all 22 pages. the report prints a last payment date, and the arithmetic measured from that date to the report's own reference date exceeds the six-calendar-year span computed from the same date. that is an arithmetic result only. Whether the provision applied to this debt, whether the printed date is true, and whether the agency did anything the law forbids are all separate questions this unit does not answer. the recorded classification limits this unit to observation; no finding class is available to it and the packet is ineligible.. the exception, timing and applicability qualifications the rule record requires, carried verbatim and in full. The recorded legal source states the provision as in force but records no commencement date for it. No record in this workspace establishes when this six-year retention provision took effect, or that it applied to this debt at the relevant time. This statement therefore reports what the report prints and what the arithmetic returns; it does not state that the provision applied to the debt, and it makes no claim about statutory timing. The recorded classification for this provision is observation-only and packet-ineligible. No violation and no probable violation may be asserted or implied from this result. The reference date is exactly six years after the stated last payment date. The recorded legal text does not state whether that day falls inside or outside the period, so no result is given for this day. This result rests on one byte-pinned consumer disclosure and on two printed fields within it. It is not a statement about any other report, product, bureau, print date or format. the extraction does not prove that the payment occurred and no statement may say it did.
